state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process`, `Core\Process\Handle` and `Core\Process\Result` are green: `Result` has its class card (`RESULT_CARD`), its three member cards are in the plain voice, and `exitCode`, `stdout` and `stderr` have all their feature proofs. `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

`nvs agent show <Class>` now prints a class's `ClassDoc` prose above its members (`crates/nvs-cli/src/agent.rs`'s `push_class_card`). Before this, no class card reached the binary's help.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL. Put the commands in a script under `.agent-tmp/` and start it with `wsl.exe -- bash -lc "bash <script>"`. In the script, build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build --bin nvs` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, run `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file> 2>&1`, and write the `.out` with Write from what it printed. The attacks and benches run on both platforms: they pick `/bin/sh` or `cmd.exe` by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`. `Core\Bytes::length` returns `uint`, so a total it feeds is `uint` and an array index made from it is `(... ) as int`. `as string` over bytes that are not UTF-8 throws `RuntimeError`.

The driver's last sweep reported `proofs: Core\IO (2/2)` red with a bare `exit 1`. Re-run at the start of this session, it was green with nothing owed and no failure, so it read as a one-off rather than a regression.
